rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Three of the file's four forcing functions sit correctly inside their fences (extract-the-task-shaping-rule-1 closes 'stop and ask which one I want to rewrite and which one I want to reject... wait for my answer'; -3 closes 'Don't propose code today'; -4 forces the strong-signal/guess/unverifiable split and forbids inferring from the URL). The fourth is the @import wiring decision at 'Wire the file in, check the wording': 'If Claude picked a path outside the three, ask for that @import line before you move on. Without it the file sits on disk unread.' Reading -2's fence in isolation (the diagnostic the rule specifies) does not surface this ask — it lives only in body prose, and the maintainer block's own artefact-contracts stake (M4's walk-and-fill audit subagent cannot see the file without the @import wire) confirms it is load-bearing, not cosmetic. The maintainer block names this as a standing, deliberately-held-open gap (reaffirmed 2026-08-02, logged in pre-cohort-todos.md 2026-07-26) that keeps the wiring decision a student choice rather than a silent auto-wire, and states plainly that 'a pedagogy REVISE here is the expected steady state, not a new finding.' This judge's read agrees with that framing — see fix_hint.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: No action recommended from this lens: the maintainer block already logs this gap as accepted-by-design pending a cohort-run trigger ('fires if a cohort run shows a student picking a non-auto-load path and missing the wire'). Folding the @import ask into extract-the-task-shaping-rule-2.md's fence now, before that trigger, is explicitly against the maintainer's stated grounds.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No authored conversation, pause, or comparison cue anywhere in the body — no 'discuss with', 'tell the room', 'share with the person next to you'. Every sentence (rule-naming, story-ticket read, location choice, wiring, automation shapes) is about the artifact or the student's own move with the agent, never about cohort management.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; mood-floor (8+/10 per beat, <7 REVISE, 7 = facilitator-premium flag) applies to teaching beats only.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer Meta block names the mood target verbatim ('the rule sits in MY file at MY location... I'm not building it today — and that's the move'). All three grouped beats are teaching beats (rule-naming + reject/rewrite + story-ticket read; location decision + wiring; automation-shapes read), so the mood-floor applies throughout — no setup/launch beat to exempt. Regenerated trace scores 8/7/8 across phases and 8 at close: no beat drops below 7, so no REVISE under this rule. Phase 2 ('Wire the file in, check the wording') lands at 7 — a facilitator-premium gap, not a floor violation; what would take it to 8 is the very @import forcing-function change the pedagogy §16 finding above explicitly declines to recommend, so this gap is accepted alongside that one.

No shame-framing in student-facing body. 'The generic rule is the tell... needs rewriting into your words, or rejecting' frames the generic rule as an expected artifact to sharpen, not a mistake the student made. The wiring Note frames an un-wired file as inert plumbing ('sits on disk unread'), not a student error. Diagnostic/watch-for language stays confined to the maintainer block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check (consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, and mood-doesn't-resolve-early into one verdict).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run check: PASS — the file explicitly refuses to name a skill in Phase 2 ('Phase 2 names a `.md` file, NOT a skill. M3 Ex3 owns first skill-by-name authoring') and refuses to build automation in Phase 3 ('Don't propose code today'), matching the private strategy doc's own non-front-running boundary at M3. Module-to-module arc: PASS — the Arc block hands off to `lectures/where-the-rule-could-live.md`, matching the strategy doc's own sequencing ('Mini-lecture — where the rule could live... meta-frame closer'). Big Idea fidelity: PASS — 'find a place for your rules' matches the strategy doc's framing of the second exercise as a capture-your-world beat with a student-picked location. Mood-doesn't-resolve-early: PASS — M2 is a grounded-competence module with no downstream unease to protect. The facet that fails is strategy-fidelity itself: `content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md` § 'M2 in detail' (read 2026-08-12, file mtime same day, BEFORE the exercise's story-ticket commits later that day) states plainly 'What M2 no longer carries. The ticket-conventions read and the *refinement* term both belong to M1's `close-the-ticket`. M2 does not re-earn either, issues no homework, and its Phase 3 ends at the automation-shapes read.' The shipped file now runs exactly that move — a ticket-conventions read, via extract-the-task-shaping-rule-4 on a story ticket — inside Phase 1, before the file's own Phase 3. The module file (`plan-mode-done-right.md` line 99) already documents this as a deliberate, maintainer-directed 2026-08-12 addition ('The ticket read is no longer M1's alone... 2026-08-12, maintainer-directed'), so the addition itself is not in question — but the private strategy doc, which is the canonical arc/sequencing source per `curriculum/CLAUDE.md`'s Alignment rule ('Strategy and module file change in the same edit. Drift = process bug.'), was not updated in the same pass and still asserts the opposite boundary.
